rationale:
Decision: split into 8 children. Five are comparator-accepted declarations reused with identical frozen types; the runtime shares them by lean_name and provisions no new worker. Three are new obligations. The selected node is at depth 4 (max_depth 6), so the new children sit at depth 5. Limits: max_children 12, max_nodes 5000, current DAG 2327 nodes.

Why split. The supplied proof is Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.15, i.e. the sequential Banach–Alaoglu argument (book/chapter-06.txt lines 308–331, used for Theorem 3.11 at lines 880–891). Most of its steps are already comparator-accepted DAG declarations. What remains is three short, independent, reusable lemmas, each extracted from one step of the supplied proof.
- Step 1 is the evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ s·M_W(T); that is exactly eval_mass_bound (cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn). The comparison |α| ≤ N‖α‖ from the Notation paragraph is the third conjunct of norm_props (rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props).
  The new child local_bound packages (1.1) for an arbitrary compact K, in the operator-norm form that the approximation and continuity lemmas consume. It takes W := ball(0, R) ⊇ K, which is open and bounded, and c := N·(⨆_j M_W(T_j)).toReal.
- Step 2 (countable sup-norm-dense families of test forms with support control, by separability of C(K, Λⁿ)) is testform_dense (dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx) with U := univ. Its accepted proof is the same separability argument on a compact exhaustion. It also approximates dω; the assembly drops that clause.
- Step 3 (Tychonoff, first countability of ℝ^D, IsCompact.tendsto_subseq) is diagonal_subseq (codim1_zsl_pc_diagonal_subseq) with ι := D.
- Step 4 (the ε/3 Cauchy argument) is the new child dense_extension.
- Step 5 (linearity by uniqueness of limits, the limit bound, sequential continuity) is the new child limit_current. Its continuity part is order_zero_current (cmcs_rc_order_zero_current).
- Step 6 is the assembly below.

Without the split, the parent would have to re-prove steps 2–3 and the continuity estimate, duplicating accepted work; testform_dense alone needed three accepted children. dense_extension and limit_current are stated for arbitrary sequences of currents in ℝ^P, so they are directly reusable, for example by the queued twin node dimred_mbl_tc_weak_compactness. Its ball-only mass hypothesis would need a massOn_mono adapter before it could use local_bound. No child proves another DAG node's statement.

Parent assembly. This proves the selected statement from the children and is compiled in Lean.
1. local_bound applied to (T_j) gives, for every compact K, a c_K ≥ 0 with |T_j(ω)| ≤ c_K·s whenever tsupport ω ⊆ K and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s for all x.
2. testform_dense with U := univ (isOpen_univ) gives a countable D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P). For each ω it also gives a compact K ⊇ tsupport ω and forms ω_k ∈ D with tsupport ω_k ⊆ K and ω_k → ω uniformly. The clauses K ⊆ univ and dω_k → dω are not used.
3. Let δ ∈ D. δ is continuous with compact support, so there is s_δ with ‖δ(x)‖ ≤ s_δ for all x (Continuous.bounded_above_of_compact_support), and K := tsupport δ is compact (HasCompactSupport.isCompact). Step 1 gives |T_j(δ)| ≤ c_K·s_δ =: M_δ for every j.
4. Apply diagonal_subseq with ι := ↥D (Countable by Set.Countable.to_subtype), b_δ(j) := T_j(δ) and M. This gives a strictly increasing σ such that T_{σ(i)}(δ) converges for every δ ∈ D.
5. S_i := T_{σ(i)} inherits the bounds of step 1 (take j := σ(i)).
6. dense_extension, with hypotheses (a), (b), (c) supplied by steps 5, 2 and 4, gives convergence of S_i(ω) for every test form ω.
7. limit_current, with hypotheses supplied by steps 5 and 6, gives C ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n with WeaklyConvergesOn S C.
8. φ := σ and C prove the selected statement.

Citations.
- Simon, Introduction to Geometric Measure Theory, Ch. 6, 2.13–2.15 and 3.11.
- The sequential Banach–Alaoglu (Helly) theorem: every bounded sequence in the dual of a separable normed space has a pointwise convergent subsequence. Its proof diagonalizes on a countable dense set and then extends by boundedness, which is exactly diagonal_subseq followed by dense_extension. Sources: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Banach%E2%80%93Alaoglu_theorem (sequential version) and Royden–Fitzpatrick, Real Analysis, §8.3 Weak Sequential Compactness (notes at https://faculty.etsu.edu/gardnerr/5210/notes/8-3.pdf); Simon cites [Roy88] for this step.

subproblems.title: Evaluation bound |T(ω)| ≤ r·M_W(T) when tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω| ≤ r (fact (E1)) (reuse of the accepted declaration cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U, W ⊆ ℝ^P be arbitrary sets, let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n), ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n) and r ∈ ℝ. Write |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞]. By Simon 6.2.5, M_W(T) is the supremum of ofReal T(φ) over φ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport φ ⊆ W and |φ(x)| ≤ 1 for all x. If M_W(T) ≠ ∞, tsupport ω ⊆ W and |ω(x)| ≤ r for every x ∈ ℝ^P, then |T(ω)| ≤ r·(M_W(T)).toReal.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (ω : TestFormOn U n) (r : ℝ), T.massOn W ≠ ∞ → tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ W → (∀ x, covectorEuclideanNorm ((ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) ≤ r) → |T ω| ≤ r * (T.massOn W).toReal
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.mass_representation-a1.eval_mass_bound-a1, accepted candidate commit 7a706164baaf42fc7f55751247396a8836928310) with the identical frozen Lean type; no new child worker is provisioned. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim below.

Source: parent proof, elementary fact (E1).
1. (Homogeneity.) Let t ∈ ℝ and α be an n-covector. Then (t•α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I) for every I : Fin n → Fin P, so Σ_I [StrictMono I]((t•α)(e_I))² = t²·S with S := Σ_I [StrictMono I](α(e_I))² ≥ 0. Hence |t•α| = √(t²S) = |t|·√S = |t|·|α|. Also |α| ≥ 0, being a square root, and |−α| = |α| (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg).
2. (r ≥ 0.) By hypothesis 0 ≤ |ω(0)| ≤ r.
3. Put M := T.massOn W and m := M.toReal ≥ 0. Since M ≠ ∞, for every real a, ENNReal.ofReal a ≤ M implies a ≤ m (ENNReal.ofReal_le_iff_le_toReal).
4. (Admissible rescalings.) Fix ε > 0 and let s := r + ε > 0. Let ω' := s⁻¹ • ω, an element of TestFormOn U n (a submodule) whose underlying form is x ↦ s⁻¹•ω(x). Then tsupport ω' ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ W, since the tsupport of a scalar multiple is contained in the tsupport. By step 1, |ω'(x)| = s⁻¹|ω(x)| ≤ r/s ≤ 1 for all x. Hence ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W. Likewise −ω' ∈ massAdmissibleOn U n W, since it has the same tsupport and |−ω'(x)| = |ω'(x)|.
5. (Bound.) By GeometricCurrentOn.le_massOn, ofReal(T ω') ≤ M and ofReal(T(−ω')) ≤ M. By step 3, T ω' ≤ m and −T ω' = T(−ω') ≤ m (T is linear), i.e. |T ω'| ≤ m. By linearity T ω' = s⁻¹·T ω, so |T ω| = s·|T ω'| ≤ (r + ε)·m.
6. (Conclusion.) Since ε > 0 is arbitrary and m ≥ 0, |T ω| ≤ r·m = r·(T.massOn W).toReal.
proof_key_steps: For ε > 0, both ±(r+ε)⁻¹ω are admissible for M_W(T).
le_massOn and M_W(T) ≠ ∞ give |T ω| ≤ (r+ε)·M_W(T).toReal.
Let ε → 0.

subproblems.title: The Euclidean coefficient norm of n-covectors is a continuous seminorm dominated by the operator norm (reuse of the accepted declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let F := Covector (Euclid P) n (continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P with the operator norm ‖·‖), and let N := covectorEuclideanNorm, i.e. N(α) = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2} for the standard orthonormal basis (e_j) of ℝ^P. Then (i) N(α + α') ≤ N(α) + N(α') for all α, α' ∈ F; (ii) N(t·α) = |t|·N(α) for all t ∈ ℝ and α ∈ F; (iii) there is a real C ≥ 0 with N(α) ≤ C·‖α‖ for all α ∈ F; and (iv) N : F → ℝ is continuous.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ), (∀ α α' : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm (α + α') ≤ covectorEuclideanNorm α + covectorEuclideanNorm α') ∧ (∀ (t : ℝ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), covectorEuclideanNorm (t • α) = |t| * covectorEuclideanNorm α) ∧ (∃ C : ℝ, 0 ≤ C ∧ ∀ α : Covector (Euclid P) n, covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ C * ‖α‖) ∧ Continuous (fun α : Covector (Euclid P) n => covectorEuclideanNorm α)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props (node root.regular_set_dense-a1.mass_eq_weight-a1.test_form_approx-a1.norm_props-a1, accepted candidate commit f492ba4a003c8f1324077e050d48667ae23c7100) with the identical frozen Lean type; no new child worker is provisioned. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim below.

Source: parent proof, step 1 (Properties of N), with all details filled in.

Notation. e_j := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ j (j ∈ Fin P) is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P, so ‖e_j‖ = 1. 𝓙 is the finite type of all maps I : Fin n → Fin P, and #𝓙 = Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P). For I ∈ 𝓙, e_I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}), in Lean (fun i => e (I i)). F := Covector (Euclid P) n carries the operator norm ‖·‖ of continuous alternating maps. By definition
N(α) := covectorEuclideanNorm α = √(Σ_{I∈𝓙} q_I(α)), where q_I(α) := α(e_I)² if I is strictly increasing and q_I(α) := 0 otherwise.

1. Coefficient vector. For α ∈ F and I ∈ 𝓙 put c_I(α) := α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, and c_I(α) := 0 otherwise. Since (if p then a else 0)² = (if p then a² else 0), q_I(α) = c_I(α)² for every I. Let v(α) ∈ EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙 be the vector with coordinates c_I(α); in Lean, v α := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun I => c_I α). The Euclidean norm formula ‖w‖ = √(Σ_I ‖w_I‖²) (EuclideanSpace.norm_eq), together with ‖w_I‖² = w_I², gives
   N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for every α ∈ F.   (∗)

2. Linearity of v. Evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in the form: (α + α')(e_I) = α(e_I) + α'(e_I) and (t·α)(e_I) = t·α(e_I). So, coordinatewise, c_I(α + α') = c_I(α) + c_I(α') and c_I(t·α) = t·c_I(α); both sides are 0 when I is not strictly increasing. Hence v(α + α') = v(α) + v(α') and v(t·α) = t·v(α) (WithLp.toLp_add, WithLp.toLp_smul).

3. Proof of (i). By (∗), step 2 and the triangle inequality in EuclideanSpace ℝ 𝓙:
   N(α + α') = ‖v(α) + v(α')‖ ≤ ‖v(α)‖ + ‖v(α')‖ = N(α) + N(α').

4. Proof of (ii). By (∗), step 2 and homogeneity of the norm:
   N(t·α) = ‖t·v(α)‖ = |t|·‖v(α)‖ = |t|·N(α).

5. Coordinate bound. For every I ∈ 𝓙, |c_I(α)| ≤ ‖α‖.
   - If I is strictly increasing, the operator-norm bound for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) gives |α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_k ‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖·1 = ‖α‖.
   - Otherwise |c_I(α)| = 0 ≤ ‖α‖.

6. Proof of (iii). Put C := √(#𝓙) ≥ 0. By step 5, c_I(α)² = |c_I(α)|² ≤ ‖α‖² for every I, so Σ_I c_I(α)² ≤ #𝓙·‖α‖². Since √ is monotone and ‖α‖ ≥ 0,
   N(α) = √(Σ_I c_I(α)²) ≤ √(#𝓙·‖α‖²) = √(#𝓙)·√(‖α‖²) = C·‖α‖.

7. Proof of (iv). Let α, α' ∈ F.
   - By (i), N(α) = N((α − α') + α') ≤ N(α − α') + N(α').
   - α' − α = −(α − α') and N(−β) = N(β) (covectorEuclideanNorm_neg, or (ii) with t = −1). So by (i), N(α') = N((α' − α) + α) ≤ N(α' − α) + N(α) = N(α − α') + N(α).
   Together with (iii), |N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C·‖α − α'‖. Thus dist(N(α), N(α')) ≤ C·dist(α, α') for all α, α', so N is Lipschitz with the nonnegative constant C (LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul with K := ⟨C, C ≥ 0⟩), hence continuous.

Steps 3, 4, 6 and 7 prove (i)–(iv), with the constant C of (iii) equal to √(Fintype.card (Fin n → Fin P)).

Lean note. A compiled route (about 70 lines, no extra imports):
- Use `classical`, and define c and v with `let`.
- Prove (∗) by `rw [EuclideanSpace.norm_eq]; unfold covectorEuclideanNorm; congr 1`, then `Finset.sum_congr rfl` with `by_cases hI : StrictMono I` and `simp`.
- Prove linearity by `simp only [v, ← WithLp.toLp_add]` (resp. `← WithLp.toLp_smul`), then `congr 1; funext I; by_cases hI : StrictMono I <;> simp [c, hI]`.
- For step 5, use `α.le_opNorm (fun i => e (I i))` followed by `simpa [Real.norm_eq_abs]`; simp knows that basis vectors have norm 1.
- For step 6, use `Real.sqrt_sq`, `Real.sqrt_mul`, `Real.sqrt_le_sqrt`, `Finset.sum_le_sum` and `pow_le_pow_left₀`.
- For step 7, first rewrite N(α' − α) = N(α − α') by `rw [← neg_sub, covectorEuclideanNorm_neg]`, then apply (i) together with `sub_add_cancel`, `abs_le` and `linarith`. Finish with `(LipschitzWith.of_dist_le_mul (K := ⟨_, Real.sqrt_nonneg _⟩) hlip).continuous`.
proof_key_steps: Write N(α) = ‖v(α)‖ for the coefficient vector v(α) = (α(e_I) if I is strictly increasing, else 0)_I in EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n → Fin P).
v is additive and ℝ-homogeneous, because evaluation at a fixed tuple is linear in α.
(i) and (ii) follow from the triangle inequality and homogeneity of the Euclidean norm.
|α(e_I)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖e_{I(k)}‖ = ‖α‖, so N(α) ≤ √(card(Fin n → Fin P))·‖α‖, which is (iii).
|N(α) − N(α')| ≤ N(α − α') ≤ C‖α − α'‖, so N is Lipschitz and hence continuous, which is (iv).

subproblems.title: A countable family of test forms that is C¹-sequentially dense in 𝒟ⁿ(U) with common compact supports (reuse of the accepted declaration dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let U ⊆ ℝ^P be open. Then there is a countable set D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U) (TestFormOn U n: C^∞ compactly supported n-forms on ℝ^P whose topological support lies in U) with the following property. For every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) there are a compact set K ⊆ U with tsupport ω ⊆ K and a sequence (ω_k)_{k∈ℕ} in D such that tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for every k, ω_k → ω uniformly on ℝ^P, and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P. Here d = exteriorDerivative, and uniform convergence of covector-valued maps is with respect to the operator norm of covectors (the norm of Covector (Euclid P) k).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)), IsOpen U → ∃ D : Set (TestFormOn U n), D.Countable ∧ ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, ∃ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn U n), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ U ∧ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K ∧ (∀ k, ωs k ∈ D) ∧ (∀ k, tsupport (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K) ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) atTop ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => exteriorDerivative (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (exteriorDerivative (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n)) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration dor_lmbs_testForm_countable_approx (node root.density_one_implies_regular-a1.limsup_mass_bound-a1.slicing-a1.testform_dense-a1, accepted candidate commit b7ecbda9150d7985c7094c40f6aebfb81c4ec24b) with the identical frozen Lean type; no new child worker is provisioned. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim below.

Source: step 6(a) of the parent proof ("Such a family exists by separability of C¹_c on each compact piece of an exhaustion"), which makes precise Simon's "by considering a countable dense set of ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U)" in the proof of Ch. 6, 4.5(2) (chapter-06.txt lines 1318–1322). Notation: Λ^k := Covector (ℝ^P) k with its operator norm, a finite-dimensional normed space; ‖η‖_∞ := sup_{x∈ℝ^P} ‖η(x)‖.

1. Exhaustion of U. If U = ∅, then 𝒟ⁿ(U) = {0} (tsupport ω ⊆ ∅ forces ω = 0), and D := {0}, K := ∅, ω_k := 0 work. Assume U ≠ ∅.
 - For i ≥ 1 let K_i := {x ∈ ℝ^P : |x| ≤ i and dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) ≥ 1/i}. If U = ℝ^P, read the distance condition as void, so K_i is the closed ball B̄_i(0).
 - K_i is closed and bounded, hence compact, and K_i ⊆ U.
 - K_i ⊆ int K_{i+1}: the open set {x : |x| < i + 1, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 1/(i+1)} contains K_i and is contained in K_{i+1}.
 - ⋃_i K_i = U, because for x ∈ U, dist(x, ℝ^P ∖ U) > 0 (U is open).
 - Consequently every compact C ⊆ U lies in some K_i: the increasing open sets int K_{i+1} cover C, so finitely many do, hence one does.

2. The pieces X_i. Let X_i := {ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) : tsupport ω ⊆ K_i}. Each X_i contains 0.
 - For ω ∈ X_i, ω vanishes on the open set ℝ^P ∖ tsupport ω, so dω vanishes there too. Hence tsupport dω ⊆ tsupport ω ⊆ K_i.
 - Equip X_i with the metric d_i(ω, η) := ‖ω − η‖_∞ + ‖dω − dη‖_∞. This is finite because ω − η and dω − dη are continuous and vanish off the compact K_i.

3. Isometric embedding into a separable space.
 - Let Y_i := C(K_i, Λⁿ) × C(K_i, Λ^{n+1}), with the metric given by the sum of the two uniform metrics. Since K_i is a compact metric space and Λⁿ, Λ^{n+1} are finite-dimensional, each C(K_i, Λ^k) is a separable metric space. In Mathlib: ContinuousMap.instSeparableSpace or ContinuousMap.instSecondCountableTopology for a compact second-countable domain, from Mathlib.Topology.ContinuousMap.SecondCountableSpace, which must be added to the imports. On compact domains the compact-open topology coincides with uniform convergence. Hence Y_i is a separable metric space.
 - Define Φ_i : X_i → Y_i by Φ_i(ω) := (ω|_{K_i}, (dω)|_{K_i}).
 - For ω, η ∈ X_i, both ω − η and dω − dη vanish outside K_i, so their sup over ℝ^P equals their sup over K_i. Thus Φ_i is an isometry from (X_i, d_i) onto its image.

4. Countable dense subsets. Every subset of a separable metric space is separable. So Φ_i(X_i) has a countable dense subset, and pulling back along the isometry Φ_i gives a countable D_i ⊆ X_i with: for every ω ∈ X_i and every k ∈ ℕ there is η ∈ D_i with d_i(η, ω) < 1/(k+1).

5. The family D. Put D := ⋃_{i≥1} D_i. It is countable, as a countable union of countable sets, and D ⊆ 𝒟ⁿ(U).

6. Approximation. Let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
 - ω is a test form, so tsupport ω is compact, and tsupport ω ⊆ U. By step 1, tsupport ω ⊆ K_i for some i, so ω ∈ X_i.
 - For each k choose ω_k ∈ D_i ⊆ D with d_i(ω_k, ω) < 1/(k+1) (step 4). Put K := K_i: it is compact, K ⊆ U, tsupport ω ⊆ K, and tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for all k.
 - Then ‖ω_k − ω‖_∞ < 1/(k+1) and ‖dω_k − dω‖_∞ < 1/(k+1). So ω_k → ω and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P; in Lean this is Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff, with dist = norm of the difference in Λ^k. ∎
proof_key_steps: Compact exhaustion K_i of U with K_i ⊆ int K_{i+1}; every compact subset of U lies in some K_i.
Test forms supported in K_i embed isometrically, via ω ↦ (ω|K_i, dω|K_i), into the separable metric space C(K_i, Λⁿ) × C(K_i, Λ^{n+1}).
Choose a countable dense D_i in each piece X_i and put D = ⋃ D_i.
Given ω, pick K_i ⊇ tsupport ω and ω_k ∈ D_i within 1/(k+1); since all supports lie in K_i, ω_k → ω and dω_k → dω uniformly on ℝ^P.

subproblems.title: Common convergent subsequence for countably many bounded real sequences (diagonal extraction) (reuse of the accepted declaration codim1_zsl_pc_diagonal_subseq)
subproblems.statement: Let ι be a countable type, b : ι → ℕ → ℝ and M : ι → ℝ with |b_k(i)| ≤ M_k for all k and i. Then there is a strictly increasing σ : ℕ → ℕ such that for every k the sequence i ↦ b_k(σ(i)) converges in ℝ.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (ι : Type) [Countable ι] (b : ι → ℕ → ℝ) (M : ι → ℝ), (∀ k i, |b k i| ≤ M k) → ∃ σ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono σ ∧ ∀ k, ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => b k (σ i)) atTop (𝓝 L)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration codim1_zsl_pc_diagonal_subseq (node root.dimension_reduction_results-a1.codimension_one_regularity-a1.zero_scale_limit_plane-a1.bv_compactness-a1.diagonal_subseq-a1, accepted candidate commit 0108f79246c75f0e500c4cb4893843fa6a8c4ce7) with the identical frozen Lean type; no new child worker is provisioned. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim below.

Source. Supplied proof of the parent node, step 6: the averages lie in a compact product (isCompact_univ_pi), and IsCompact.tendsto_subseq extracts the subsequence; this is the single-extraction variant stated there. No sibling child is used.

1. Let X := ℝ^ι (functions ι → ℝ) with the product topology, and S := Π_k [−M_k, M_k] ⊆ X. Each interval is compact, so S is compact by Tychonoff (isCompact_univ_pi).
2. X is first countable, since ι is countable and ℝ is first countable (Mathlib instance for countable products).
3. The points x_i := (b_k(i))_k lie in S, because |b_k(i)| ≤ M_k.
4. In a first countable space, every sequence in a compact set has a convergent subsequence with limit in the set (IsCompact.tendsto_subseq). So there are a ∈ S and a strictly increasing σ with x_{σ(i)} → a.
5. Evaluation at k is continuous on X, so b_k(σ(i)) = x_{σ(i)}(k) → a(k) for every k. ∎
If some M_k < 0 the hypothesis is impossible, and if ι is empty the claim is trivial; both cases are covered.

Appendix (Lean proof, kernel-checked). Compiled with the pinned toolchain (Lean v4.35.0-rc3, Mathlib 25730c7c) inside namespace GMT.Ch07 of a file importing GMT.Ch07.Submission, with the contract's opens. It is one declaration with no helper declaration and no set_option. #print axioms gives propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.

theorem Submission.codim1_zsl_pc_diagonal_subseq : ∀ (ι : Type) [Countable ι] (b : ι → ℕ → ℝ) (M : ι → ℝ), (∀ k i, |b k i| ≤ M k) → ∃ σ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono σ ∧ ∀ k, ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => b k (σ i)) atTop (𝓝 L) := by
  intro ι _ b M hb
  have hS : IsCompact (Set.pi univ (fun k => Icc (-M k) (M k))) :=
    isCompact_univ_pi (fun k => isCompact_Icc)
  have hx : ∀ i, (fun k => b k i) ∈ Set.pi univ (fun k => Icc (-M k) (M k)) := by
    intro i
    rw [Set.mem_univ_pi]
    intro k
    exact Set.mem_Icc.mpr (abs_le.mp (hb k i))
  obtain ⟨a, -, σ, hσ, hlim⟩ := hS.tendsto_subseq hx
  exact ⟨σ, hσ, fun k => ⟨a k, ((continuous_apply k).tendsto a).comp hlim⟩⟩
proof_key_steps: Π_k[−M_k, M_k] is compact in ℝ^ι (Tychonoff), and ℝ^ι is first countable for countable ι.
Extract a convergent subsequence of x_i = (b_k(i))_k.
Each coordinate converges, by continuity of evaluation.

subproblems.title: A linear functional on 𝒟ⁿ(U) with zeroth-order bounds on every compact subset of U is a current (reuse of the accepted declaration cmcs_rc_order_zero_current)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let U ⊆ ℝ^P be any set, and let L : 𝒟ⁿ(U) → ℝ be ℝ-linear (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ). Suppose that for every compact K ⊆ U there is c ∈ ℝ such that |L(ω)| ≤ c·M for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x ∈ ℝ^P (‖·‖ the operator norm on n-covectors). Then there is a current S ∈ 𝒟_n(U) (GeometricCurrentOn U n, i.e. L together with Simon's sequential continuity) with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (L : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → K ⊆ U → ∃ c : ℝ, ∀ (ω : TestFormOn U n) (M : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ M) → |L ω| ≤ c * M) → ∃ S : GeometricCurrentOn U n, ∀ ω : TestFormOn U n, S ω = L ω
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse: this is the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmcs_rc_order_zero_current (node root.compactness_of_minimizing_currents-a1.slicing-a1.restrict_current-a1.order_zero_current-a1, accepted candidate commit 493589396f764fe4188e236e4a99686eee7b2614) with the identical frozen Lean type; no new child worker is provisioned. Its accepted parent-supplied proof is reproduced verbatim below.

Source: step 4 of the parent proof of cmcs_restrict_current (sequential continuity), with the integral functional S₀ replaced by an arbitrary linear functional L satisfying the zeroth-order estimate that step 4 uses for S₀.

For ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U) write ω̂ := (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) for its underlying form, and ‖·‖ for the operator norm of n-covectors.

1. (Reduction.) A GeometricCurrentOn U n is a structure ⟨T₀, h⟩ consisting of a linear map T₀ : TestFormOn U n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ and a proof h that T₀(ω_j) → 0 for every sequence (ω_j) with TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0; its value S(ω) is T₀(ω). Take T₀ := L. Then S(ω) = L(ω) holds by definition for every ω, and it remains to prove: if (ω_j)_{j∈ℕ} in 𝒟ⁿ(U) satisfies TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0, then L(ω_j) → 0 in ℝ.

2. (Unpacking the convergence.) By definition of TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 there is a compact K ⊆ U with tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K for all j such that, for every k ∈ ℕ, iteratedFDeriv ℝ k ω̂_j → iteratedFDeriv ℝ k 0̂ uniformly on K, where 0̂ is the underlying form of the zero test form, i.e. the zero function. Apply the hypothesis to this compact K ⊆ U to obtain c ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ c·M whenever ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U), tsupport ω̂ ⊆ K and ‖ω̂(x)‖ ≤ M for all x.

3. (Zeroth-order smallness on K.) For every function G and point x, ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ (norm_iteratedFDeriv_zero). In particular ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x‖ = ‖0̂(x)‖ = 0, so iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x = 0 for every x. Uniform convergence for k = 0, in metric form (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff together with eventually_atTop), says: for every η > 0 there is N such that dist(iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 0̂ x, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K. This distance equals dist(0, iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x) = ‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 ω̂_j x‖ = ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ (dist_zero_left). Hence ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ < η for all j ≥ N and all x ∈ K.

4. (Off K.) If x ∉ K, then x ∉ tsupport ω̂_j (because tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K), so ω̂_j(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport) and ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ = 0 ≤ η. With step 3: for every j ≥ N, ‖ω̂_j(x)‖ ≤ η for all x ∈ ℝ^P.

5. (Conclusion.) Let δ > 0 and put η := δ/(|c| + 1) > 0; let N be as in step 3 for this η. For j ≥ N, the hypothesis applied to ω := ω_j and M := η (valid by tsupport ω̂_j ⊆ K and step 4) gives
   |L(ω_j) − 0| = |L(ω_j)| ≤ c·η ≤ |c|·η = δ·|c|/(|c| + 1) < δ,
   using c ≤ |c|, η ≥ 0, δ > 0 and |c| < |c| + 1. Since δ > 0 was arbitrary, L(ω_j) → 0 (Metric.tendsto_atTop). This is the continuity requirement, so S := ⟨L, h⟩ is a GeometricCurrentOn U n with S(ω) = L(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(U). ∎
proof_key_steps: Take S := ⟨L, h⟩; then S(ω) = L(ω) by definition, so only L(ω_j) → 0 for TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 must be shown.
TestFormOnConverges ω_j 0 gives a compact K ⊆ U containing every tsupport ω_j and uniform convergence on K of the order-0 derivatives; take the constant c for this K.
‖iteratedFDeriv ℝ 0 G x‖ = ‖G(x)‖ and the limit form is 0, so for every η > 0 eventually ‖ω_j(x)‖ < η on K; off K, ω_j(x) = 0.
With η = δ/(|c|+1): eventually |L(ω_j)| ≤ c·η ≤ |c|·η < δ, hence L(ω_j) → 0.

subproblems.title: Uniform local mass bounds give uniform sup-norm bounds for T_j(ω) on test forms supported in a fixed compact set
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let T_j ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, j ∈ ℕ) satisfy ⨆_j M_W(T_j) < ∞ in [0, ∞] (M_W = massOn, Simon 6.2.5 with the Euclidean coefficient norm) for every bounded open W ⊆ ℝ^P. Then for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P there is a real c ≥ 0 such that |T_j(ω)| ≤ c·s for every j ∈ ℕ, every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and every s ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s for all x ∈ ℝ^P, where ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Ts : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ W : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen W → Bornology.IsBounded W → ⨆ j, (Ts j).massOn W < ∞) → ∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (j : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (s : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ s) → |Ts j ω| ≤ c * s
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 1 of the parent proof (the evaluation bound (1.1), from the definition of M_W, Simon Ch. 6, 2.5) combined with the comparison |α| ≤ N‖α‖ from the parent's Notation paragraph; the bounded open set W is a ball containing K, as the B_k of the parent proof. Siblings used: eval_mass_bound (accepted declaration cmr_abs_apply_le_massOn) and norm_props (accepted declaration rsd_mw_tfa_norm_props).

Notation. |α| := covectorEuclideanNorm α and ‖α‖ is the operator norm of α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n; M_W(T) := T.massOn W ∈ [0, ∞]; all test forms are elements of TestFormOn univ n, and ω(x) denotes the value of the underlying form.

1. (Norm comparison.) The third conjunct of norm_props for P and n gives a real N ≥ 0 with |α| ≤ N·‖α‖ for every α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n.
2. (Choice of W.) K is compact, hence bounded (IsCompact.isBounded), so there is R ∈ ℝ with K ⊆ W := ball(0, R) (Bornology.IsBounded.subset_ball with centre 0). W is open (isOpen_ball) and bounded (isBounded_ball), so the hypothesis gives m := ⨆_j M_W(T_j) < ∞.
3. (The constant.) Put c := N·m.toReal. Then c ≥ 0, because N ≥ 0 and m.toReal ≥ 0.
4. (Finite masses.) For every j, M_W(T_j) ≤ m (le_iSup), so M_W(T_j) < ∞, i.e. M_W(T_j) ≠ ∞; and, since m ≠ ∞, M_W(T_j).toReal ≤ m.toReal (ENNReal.toReal_mono).
5. (Evaluation bound.) Fix j ∈ ℕ, a test form ω with tsupport ω ⊆ K and s ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s for all x. Then s ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0. For every x, |ω(x)| ≤ N·‖ω(x)‖ ≤ N·s by step 1 and N ≥ 0. Moreover tsupport ω ⊆ K ⊆ W, and M_W(T_j) ≠ ∞ by step 4. Hence eval_mass_bound, applied with U := univ, this W, T := T_j, this ω and r := N·s, gives |T_j(ω)| ≤ N·s·M_W(T_j).toReal.
6. (Conclusion.) Since N·s ≥ 0, step 4 gives N·s·M_W(T_j).toReal ≤ N·s·m.toReal = c·s. Therefore |T_j(ω)| ≤ c·s for all j, all test forms ω with tsupport ω ⊆ K and all s with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s for every x, and c ≥ 0 by step 3. ∎
proof_key_steps: norm_props gives N ≥ 0 with covectorEuclideanNorm α ≤ N‖α‖.
Enclose K in the open bounded ball W := ball(0, R); then m := ⨆_j M_W(T_j) < ∞, and c := N·m.toReal ≥ 0.
If tsupport ω ⊆ K and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s, then |ω(x)| ≤ N·s and M_W(T_j) ≤ m < ∞, so eval_mass_bound gives |T_j(ω)| ≤ N·s·M_W(T_j).toReal ≤ c·s.

subproblems.title: Convergence on a sup-norm-dense family of test forms extends to all test forms under uniform local bounds
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, i ∈ ℕ) and let D be a set of test forms in 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n); ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n. Assume: (a) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P there is a real c ≥ 0 with |S_i(ω)| ≤ c·s for all i ∈ ℕ, all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and all s ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s for every x; (b) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) there are a compact K ⊆ ℝ^P with tsupport ω ⊆ K and a sequence (ω_k)_{k∈ℕ} with ω_k ∈ D and tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for every k, such that ω_k → ω uniformly on ℝ^P; (c) for every δ ∈ D the real sequence (S_i(δ))_{i∈ℕ} converges. Then for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) the real sequence (S_i(ω))_{i∈ℕ} converges.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (D : Set (TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n)), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (s : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ s) → |S i ω| ≤ c * s) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∃ (K : Set (Euclid P)) (ωs : ℕ → TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), IsCompact K ∧ tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K ∧ (∀ k, ωs k ∈ D) ∧ (∀ k, tsupport (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K) ∧ TendstoUniformly (fun k x => (ωs k : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x) (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) atTop) → (∀ δ ∈ D, ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => S i δ) atTop (𝓝 L)) → ∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => S i ω) atTop (𝓝 L)
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (convergence on every test form), the boundedness half of the standard proof of the sequential Banach–Alaoglu theorem that Simon invokes for Ch. 6, Lemma 2.15: convergence on a sup-norm-dense family extends to all test forms because the functionals are uniformly bounded. The approximating forms δ ∈ D_k of the parent proof are here the terms ω_k supplied by hypothesis (b). No sibling is used.

Notation. All test forms are elements of TestFormOn univ n; ω(x) is the value of the underlying form and ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n, whose metric is dist(α, β) = ‖α − β‖ (dist_eq_norm).

1. (Setup.) Fix ω. By (b) choose a compact K with tsupport ω ⊆ K and a sequence (ω_k) with ω_k ∈ D and tsupport ω_k ⊆ K for every k, and ω_k → ω uniformly on ℝ^P. By (a) choose c ≥ 0 for this K. Since ℝ is complete, a Cauchy sequence of reals converges (cauchySeq_tendsto_of_complete), so it suffices to show that (S_i(ω))_i is Cauchy, i.e. (Metric.cauchySeq_iff) that for every ε > 0 there is I with |S_i(ω) − S_l(ω)| < ε for all i, l ≥ I.
2. (Choice of the approximant.) Let ε > 0 and η := ε/(3(c + 1)) > 0. Uniform convergence (Metric.tendstoUniformly_iff) gives, eventually in k and in particular for some k, dist(ω(x), ω_k(x)) < η for all x ∈ ℝ^P. Fix such a k.
3. (Uniform closeness of the evaluations.) The test form ω − ω_k has underlying form x ↦ ω(x) − ω_k(x), so ‖(ω − ω_k)(x)‖ = dist(ω(x), ω_k(x)) ≤ η for every x, and tsupport(ω − ω_k) ⊆ tsupport ω ∪ tsupport ω_k ⊆ K (tsupport_sub). Since each S_i is linear, S_i(ω) − S_i(ω_k) = S_i(ω − ω_k). Hypothesis (a) with this K, the form ω − ω_k and s := η gives |S_i(ω) − S_i(ω_k)| ≤ c·η for every i. Finally c·η = c·ε/(3(c + 1)) < ε/3, because 0 ≤ c < c + 1 and ε > 0. Hence |S_i(ω) − S_i(ω_k)| < ε/3 for every i ∈ ℕ.
4. (Cauchy property on the approximant.) ω_k ∈ D, so by (c) the sequence (S_i(ω_k))_i converges and is therefore Cauchy: there is I with |S_i(ω_k) − S_l(ω_k)| < ε/3 for all i, l ≥ I.
5. (ε/3 estimate.) For i, l ≥ I, by the triangle inequality and steps 3–4,
   |S_i(ω) − S_l(ω)| ≤ |S_i(ω) − S_i(ω_k)| + |S_i(ω_k) − S_l(ω_k)| + |S_l(ω_k) − S_l(ω)| < ε/3 + ε/3 + ε/3 = ε.
6. (Conclusion.) Hence (S_i(ω))_i is a Cauchy sequence of reals, so there is L ∈ ℝ with S_i(ω) → L. Since ω was arbitrary, this holds for every test form ω. ∎
proof_key_steps: For ω take K and ω_k ∈ D from (b), and c ≥ 0 from (a) for this K; it suffices to show (S_i(ω)) is Cauchy.
Given ε > 0 choose k with ‖ω(x) − ω_k(x)‖ < η := ε/(3(c+1)) for all x; since tsupport(ω − ω_k) ⊆ K, linearity and (a) give |S_i(ω) − S_i(ω_k)| ≤ c·η < ε/3 for every i.
(S_i(ω_k)) converges by (c), hence is Cauchy; the ε/3 estimate shows (S_i(ω)) is Cauchy, so it converges in ℝ.

subproblems.title: The pointwise limit of currents with uniform local sup-norm bounds is a current and their weak limit
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and S_i ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n, i ∈ ℕ); ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n. Assume (a) for every compact K ⊆ ℝ^P there is a real c ≥ 0 with |S_i(ω)| ≤ c·s for all i ∈ ℕ, all ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with tsupport ω ⊆ K and all s ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ s for every x; and (b) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) the real sequence (S_i(ω))_{i∈ℕ} converges. Then there is C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) with S_i ⇀ C, i.e. S_i(ω) → C(ω) for every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (WeaklyConvergesOn S C).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (S : ℕ → GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → ∃ c : ℝ, 0 ≤ c ∧ ∀ (i : ℕ) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (s : ℝ), tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) ⊆ K → (∀ x, ‖(ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) x‖ ≤ s) → |S i ω| ≤ c * s) → (∀ ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, ∃ L : ℝ, Tendsto (fun i => S i ω) atTop (𝓝 L)) → ∃ C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, WeaklyConvergesOn S C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 5 of the parent proof (C is a current in ℝ^P): linearity of the pointwise limit by uniqueness of limits, the bound |C(ω)| ≤ c·s as the limit of the uniform bounds, and sequential continuity derived from that bound; the last part is exactly the accepted sibling order_zero_current. Sibling used: order_zero_current (accepted declaration cmcs_rc_order_zero_current).

Notation. All test forms are elements of TestFormOn univ n; ω(x) is the value of the underlying form and ‖·‖ is the operator norm on Covector (Euclid P) n.

1. (The pointwise limit.) By (b), for every test form ω choose L(ω) ∈ ℝ with S_i(ω) → L(ω) as i → ∞. Limits of real sequences are unique (tendsto_nhds_unique, ℝ is Hausdorff and atTop on ℕ is a proper filter).
2. (Additivity.) Let ω, η be test forms. Each S_i is linear, so S_i(ω + η) = S_i(ω) + S_i(η) → L(ω) + L(η) (Tendsto.add). Also S_i(ω + η) → L(ω + η) by step 1. By uniqueness of limits, L(ω + η) = L(ω) + L(η).
3. (Homogeneity.) Let a ∈ ℝ and ω a test form. Then S_i(a·ω) = a·S_i(ω) → a·L(ω) (Tendsto.const_mul), and S_i(a·ω) → L(a·ω). Hence L(a·ω) = a·L(ω). By steps 2–3, L is an ℝ-linear map TestFormOn univ n →ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
4. (Zeroth-order bounds for L.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact (trivially K ⊆ univ) and let c ≥ 0 be given by (a). Let ω be a test form with tsupport ω ⊆ K and M ∈ ℝ with ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x. By (a), |S_i(ω)| ≤ c·M for every i. By continuity of the absolute value, |S_i(ω)| → |L(ω)| (Tendsto.abs), and a limit of terms all ≤ c·M is ≤ c·M (le_of_tendsto'). Hence |L(ω)| ≤ c·M.
5. (L is a current.) Step 4 is precisely the hypothesis of order_zero_current for U := univ and the linear map L of step 3: for every compact K ⊆ univ there is c ∈ ℝ with |L(ω)| ≤ c·M whenever tsupport ω ⊆ K and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x. Therefore order_zero_current yields C ∈ GeometricCurrentOn univ n with C(ω) = L(ω) for every test form ω.
6. (Weak convergence.) For every test form ω, S_i(ω) → L(ω) = C(ω) by steps 1 and 5. This is WeaklyConvergesOn S C. ∎
proof_key_steps: Let L(ω) := lim_i S_i(ω).
Uniqueness of limits makes L ℝ-linear.
Passing to the limit in (a) gives |L(ω)| ≤ c·M when tsupport ω ⊆ K and ‖ω(x)‖ ≤ M for all x.
order_zero_current turns L into a current C with C(ω) = L(ω), so S_i(ω) → C(ω) for every ω.
